Load packages
```{r, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(misty)
```

Import raw data.
```{r, message=FALSE}
dat <- read.csv2('Data/Pilot_data_raw.csv')
```
# Variable recodings

## Dependent measures

The dependent variable was participants’ perceived frequency of healthy and tasty food in each restaurant, which we assessed in two ways: 

Participants indicated how healthy and tasty most people in their country expect the food to be in each type of restaurant, each on a slider scale from 1 = *very unhealthy/not tasty at all* to 100 = *very healthy/very tasty*. 

They also estimated the relative percentages of healthy versus unhealthy and tasty versus not tasty food in each restaurant (Base rate estimates). They indicated their estimates each on two slider scales from 0 % to 100 %, which had to amount to 100% for health and taste base rates.

We checked whether the three different measures per health and taste in each restaurant (overall health/taste rating, base rate estimate of tasty/healthy and not tasty/unhealthy food) were correlated so that they could be combined into one measure.
For this, we first reverse-coded the base rate estimates for unhealthy and not tasty foods, so that high values on all scales indicate high frequency estimates of tasty and healthy food, respectively.

```{r}
dat <- 
  dat %>% 
  mutate(base_unhealthy_1_r = item.reverse(base_unhealthy_1, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_unhealthy_2_r = item.reverse(base_unhealthy_2, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_unhealthy_3_r = item.reverse(base_unhealthy_3, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_unhealthy_4_r = item.reverse(base_unhealthy_4, min = 0, max = 100),
  )

dat <- 
  dat %>% 
  mutate(base_ntasty_1_r = item.reverse(base_ntasty_1, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_ntasty_2_r = item.reverse(base_ntasty_2, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_ntasty_3_r = item.reverse(base_ntasty_3, min = 0, max = 100),
         base_ntasty_4_r = item.reverse(base_ntasty_4, min = 0, max = 100),
  )
```

Scale reliability per restaurant type:

**Restaurant 1:** Fast-food place
```{r}
dat %>% 
  select(health_1, base_healthy_1, base_unhealthy_1_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()

dat %>% 
  select(taste_1, base_tasty_1, base_ntasty_1_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()


```

**Restaurant 2:** Street-food joint

```{r}
dat %>% 
  select(health_2, base_healthy_2, base_unhealthy_2_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()

dat %>% 
  select(taste_2, base_tasty_2, base_ntasty_2_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()

```

**Restaurant 3:** Upscale scene restaurant

```{r}
dat %>% 
  select(health_3, base_healthy_3, base_unhealthy_3_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()

dat %>% 
  select(taste_3, base_tasty_3, base_ntasty_3_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()
```

**Restaurant 4:** School or university cafeteria

```{r}
dat %>% 
  select(health_4, base_healthy_4, base_unhealthy_4_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()

dat %>% 
  select(taste_4, base_tasty_4, base_ntasty_4_r) %>% 
  item.alpha()
```

Because the average rating and the base rate estimates for healthy and tasty food were highly correlated (all Cronbach's alphas between .72 and .96), we averaged them into one measure per restaurant, indicating the estimated frequency of healthy and tasty food, respectively.

```{r}
dat <-
  dat %>% 
  mutate(health_freq1 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('health_1', 'base_healthy_1', 'base_unhealthy_1_r')]),
         health_freq2 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('health_2', 'base_healthy_2', 'base_unhealthy_2_r')]),
         health_freq3 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('health_3', 'base_healthy_3', 'base_unhealthy_3_r')]),
         health_freq4 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('health_4', 'base_healthy_4', 'base_unhealthy_4_r')]),
         taste_freq1 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('taste_1', 'base_tasty_1', 'base_ntasty_1_r')]),
         taste_freq2 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('taste_2', 'base_tasty_2', 'base_ntasty_2_r')]),
         taste_freq3 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('taste_3', 'base_tasty_3', 'base_ntasty_3_r')]),
         taste_freq4 = rowMeans(.[ ,c('taste_4', 'base_tasty_4', 'base_ntasty_4_r')])
  )

```

# Save processed data

```{r}
dat %>% 
  select(id, study_run, contains('freq')) %>% 
  write_csv2('Data/Pilot_data_processed.csv')
 
```
